title: brandkit-design-brain
universal_lens: The Design Brain formalizes a constrained optimization operator acting on a bounded information manifold. It projects high-dimensional, noisy user inputs onto a low-dimensional 'Creative DNA' subspace, enforcing strict orthogonality against generic prior distributions (clichés) to yield a unique, coherent visual state vector.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the Design Brain as a conformal inference engine over brand attributes. The 'Source of Truth' acts as the calibration set, while the Creative DNA extraction computes posterior probabilities for optimal visual axes, ensuring predictive coverage and rejecting out-of-distribution aesthetic anomalies.
gse_mapping: In GSE, this operates as a discrete Markov decision process. The system transitions from an initial brief state to a final asset state via intermediate 'Creative DNA' nodes, applying deterministic policy gradients that maximize coherence while strictly penalizing forbidden cliché states.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Brandkit Design Brain functions fundamentally as a constrained optimization manifold operating within a high-dimensional aesthetic vector space. We define the input state $I$ as the concatenation of mandatory intake answers, official assets, and reference signals. The core operator, `Compile Creative DNA`, acts as a non-linear projection matrix $P$, reducing $I$ into a lower-dimensional subspace $Y$ characterized by orthogonal axes such as Product Truth, Audience Desire, and Visual Axes. This projection is not merely compressive but highly selective, governed by a strict loss function $L$. The loss function heavily penalizes proximity to known 'Generic AI-branding clichés', effectively creating repulsive potential fields around high-density regions of平庸 (mediocre) design space. Furthermore, the system enforces hard constraints—such as 'Do not copy a supplied reference'—which act as boundary conditions preventing the solution from collapsing into trivial copies of the input. The subsequent stages, like `REVISE_FROM_FEEDBACK`, operate as localized gradient descents on this manifold. When a user provides feedback targeting a specific element (e.g., palette), the system calculates the partial derivative of the overall coherence metric with respect to that element, adjusting it while simultaneously re-evaluating downstream dependencies (e.g., typography contrast). This ensures that the final output—a coherent Essential Kit—is a stable equilibrium point where all visual vectors are collinear with the central mechanism. Failure modes arise when the input manifold is too sparse (under-specified brief), leading to rank-deficient projections, or when the anti-cliché regularization is overly aggressive, pushing the solution into non-producible, chaotic geometric regimes.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The Design Brain models a dual-agent adversarial dynamic. Agent A (the Brand) seeks to project a unique, ownable identity that maximizes signal-to-noise ratio in the consumer's mind. Agent B (the Market/Competition) exerts pressure toward homogenization, pulling the brand toward safe, generic clichés. The Design Brain acts as the strategic optimizer for Agent A, anticipating Agent B's predictable moves (generic leaves, sparkles) and proactively deploying distinctive, counter-intuitive visual mechanisms to secure a defensible position in the perceptual landscape.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists at the intersection of the 'Central Mechanism' and the 'Forbidden Clichés'. If the proposed central visual idea exhibits high collinearity with any vector in the forbidden set, the system must trigger a hard rejection, regardless of how well it satisfies the immediate brief. Additionally, leakage vetoes occur if the internal 'Creative DNA' analysis is exposed to the user; the abstraction layer must remain perfectly opaque to preserve the illusion of intuitive, effortless generation, preventing cognitive dissonance in the end-user experience.
